source_integrity.duplicate_code_result: Unique vendor I2C bridge case; host i2c-tools and inventory reads are not equivalent.

source_snapshot.procedure_and_criteria: OEM 0x30/0x25 leaves bus, address, count and write data as placeholders and accepts success only.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES verified command mapping and byte-exact transaction.

historical_reviews.history: No related read authorizes arbitrary I2C access.

original_test_intent: Perform one approved bounded I2C transaction to a known BMC bus/device/register and verify ACK, count and device response.
original_method: Preserve OEM command intent and source; do not run until every byte is approved.
manual_activity: Platform owner approves topology, address convention, device protocol, exact transaction and recovery.
engineer_actions: Approve schema/target/recovery and own DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Recognizes missing data but is not runnable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Submit one allowlisted byte-exact transaction and validate device-specific response.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind command to topology and slave protocol, validate ACK/length/content and restore any changed register.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds schema, bounds and recovery in Review only.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Standard 0x06/0x52 is an override unless OEM equivalence is proven.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong bytes can alter power, clocks or EEPROM.

project_override_considerations: Alternate tools require byte/effect equivalence and disclosure of unverified OEM coverage.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source is an unconstrained bus transaction with placeholder bytes and a success-only criterion.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Vendor/project inputs can make the operation ready.

review_improvement: Converts arbitrary bus access into one allowlisted protocol transaction.
independent_technical_reasoning: I2C behavior depends on topology and slave protocol, not only bus/address. OEM opcode ambiguity and unconstrained writes create board-level risk, so exact approved bytes and a device-specific oracle are mandatory.
